structured.approach: I followed the data-science-steps procedure for DS-06 and read both contracted inputs: task.code, which lists the DS-05 changes C-1 to C-3 and the planned tests C-4 and C-5, and feat.stories, which has AC-03.1 to AC-03.8 and AC-04.1 to AC-04.5. I called the CodeGraph MCP tool (codegraph_explore with the ap_forecast projectPath) to read the exact source of vendor_risk, build_explanation_request, load_config and predict_delay_days and to see which tests cover them. I read ci.py to see the coverage gate. feat.stories SA-6 allows new test files, so the tests are in two new files: tests/test_risk.py for STORY-03 and tests/test_explain_risk.py for STORY-04. tests/test_forecast.py is unchanged. Each acceptance criterion maps to at least one named test. The boundary days 30 and 10 are tested explicitly (lesson L-007), along with rounded-prediction cases, a generator input and the no-LLM, no-config isolation (patched load_config and an AST import check). I ran the full suite through `/usr/bin/python3 ci.py`, and it passed. I then rewrote task.unit_tests.md in full with the AC-to-test map, the CI results, what is deliberately left untested and the open questions carried forward. No source files were changed and nothing was committed.

claims.text: The repository CI gates coverage of src/ap_forecast at COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0 and also checks compile, unit tests and static issues.
`/usr/bin/python3 ci.py` passes with compile true, 25 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors, coverage 100.0 and no static issues.
Each module has 100% line coverage: __init__.py 5 statements, explain.py 11, predict.py 5, risk.py 11, 32 in total with 0 missed.
CodeGraph's blast radius shows tests/test_risk.py covering vendor_risk, and tests/test_forecast.py and tests/test_explain_risk.py covering build_explanation_request.

vendor_risk returns 'high' above HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30, 'medium' above MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 and 'low' otherwise, using strict '>' on predict_delay_days(history). The tests check exactly 30 → 'medium' and exactly 10 → 'low' (AC-03.2, AC-03.4).
AC-03.7 (no LLM call, no network call, no models.json read) is tested by patching load_config and build_explanation_request to raise, and by checking that risk.py imports only typing and .predict.

AC-04.1 to AC-04.5 are each covered in tests/test_explain_risk.py: risk is appended as ' Risk level: <risk>.'; with no risk or risk=None the dict is unchanged; a positional config still binds to config; and provider, model and max_tokens come from the config or models.json.
A lane may add new unit tests in new test files instead of the existing test_forecast.py (SA-6).
This step may change only tests/, and the tests were added under tests/ only.
The version 0.10.0 is not tested, because it is still open as DSQ-1 for the Developer.

open_questions: DSQ-1 (non-blocking, Developer): confirm 0.10.0 as the minor version step from 0.9.0. No test pins the version until this is confirmed.
DSQ-2 (non-blocking, Developer): the coverage gate is met in DS-06 (100.0 against 90.0). Please confirm this closes DSQ-2.
PQ-1, TQ-4, TQ-5 (non-blocking, PM / Architect): the tests for AC-03.5, AC-03.6 and AC-04.5 follow the interim design. If an answer differs, only those tests change.
TQ-8 and PQ-5 (non-blocking, Architect / PM): whether the risk label may be sent to acme-llm, and the order of this change relative to PROV-ACME-2026-11. Both are carried unchanged.
SSQ-2 (non-blocking): confirmation of secrets access in each environment. The tests need no secret and no network.
structured.summary: Unit tests for STORY-03 (vendor_risk) and STORY-04 (the risk parameter) are in two new files, tests/test_risk.py and tests/test_explain_risk.py, and each acceptance criterion maps to a named test. The boundary days 30 and 10 are tested explicitly. The CI passes: 25 tests with 0 failures, 100.0% coverage against the 90.0 gate, and no static issues. task.unit_tests.md has been rewritten in full. No source changes were made and nothing was committed.
